sketches.title: The Ceremony That Almost Worked
sketches.premise: A wedding day begins with one small hitch, and the host turns it into a growing chain of fixes. Take turns adding the next thing someone does to keep the ceremony moving; make it clever, costly, and wonderfully overconfident.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it adds exactly the next cause-and-fix step, fits every named person, object, time, and problem, and does not skip the needed link, declare the ceremony finished, or undo an earlier fix.
sketches.move_shape: Name one immediate fix and its result, such as: “The ring slips under the piano, so the flower girl blocks the aisle while the best man crawls after it.” The points go to the trouble, pride, or blame the move puts on the other player.
sketches.first_card: The music starts, but the groom is still outside.

sketches.title: The Guest Book of Last Words
sketches.premise: Guests leave notes as the wedding day goes wrong, and each turn adds the next note in one shared guest book. Build a trail from the first hitch toward the reception, making every message fit the evidence already on the page.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it is the next believable note caused by what the book already says, names a detail that can be checked later, and does not jump over a needed event, close the book early, or erase an earlier note.
sketches.move_shape: Add one guest-book entry with its writer and reason, such as: “Aunt May writes, ‘I moved the cake because the rain came through the roof.’” The points go to the sharpest accusation, excuse, or secret the move leaves for the other player.
sketches.first_card: The guest book is open, but the first page has vanished.

sketches.title: The Seating Plan Falls Apart
sketches.premise: A wedding seating chart has one bad seat, and every turn must make the next seating change. Keep one shared chart alive while causing the grandest harmless trouble for the other player.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it changes exactly one seat because of the current chart and stated wedding facts, leaves all other seats intact, and does not skip a swap, end the seating, or put anyone back in a seat the chart already rejected.
sketches.move_shape: Move one guest and give the immediate reason, such as: “Move Uncle Ben from Table 3 to Table 1 because he can no longer see the cake.” The points go to the awkward neighbor, lost honor, or fresh duty the move forces on the other player.
sketches.first_card: The bride’s great-aunt is seated beside the one guest she refuses to greet.

sketches.title: The Cake Climbs Back
sketches.premise: The wedding cake is built one layer at a time after the first hitch. Take turns adding exactly the next layer or support, keeping the whole cake possible while making the other player’s job harder and more ridiculous.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it adds one physically supported next piece that fits the cake’s size, tools, room, and earlier choices; a skipped link is an unsupported leap, an ending is serving the cake, and an undo is removing or replacing a named piece.
sketches.move_shape: Add one layer, support, or visible decoration with its reason, such as: “A cardboard ring goes under the lemon layer because the middle has begun to sink.” The points go to the wobble, stain, burden, or public blame the move hands to the other player.
sketches.first_card: The bottom cake layer is ready, but the cake board is too small.

sketches.title: The Song Before the Vows
sketches.premise: The wedding procession is trapped in a music problem: one shared playlist must carry everyone from the first entrance to the vows. Add the next song choice and the reason it follows, while giving the other player a musical mess to manage.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it names exactly the next song or sound and a reason it follows the current scene, respects the people and instruments already present, and does not skip an entrance, finish the procession, or cancel a song already played.
sketches.move_shape: Name one next track and its immediate effect, such as: “The organ changes to a march because the flower girl has found the aisle at last.” The points go to the wrong mood, impossible request, or awkward entrance the move creates for the other player.
sketches.first_card: The first entrance is ready, but the speaker plays the couple’s shopping list.

sketches.title: The Toast Nobody Planned
sketches.premise: A wedding toast starts with one missing fact, and each turn adds the next sentence to one shared speech. Keep the speech true to the day while making the other speaker carry a bigger, brighter, more embarrassing promise.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it is exactly the next sentence that follows from the speech and wedding facts already standing, without skipping its needed setup, ending the toast, or taking back a claim already made.
sketches.move_shape: Add one sentence that follows from the last sentence, such as: “Because the bride once returned his lost shoe, the best man now promises to guard every shoe at the reception.” The points go to the public promise, risky praise, or duty the move places on the other player.
sketches.first_card: The speaker raises the glass, but cannot remember how the couple met.
